title: Past and present goals are represented concurrently during visual search
experiments_summary: The study applied multivariate EEG decoding analyses to data from two previously published visual search experiments. Experiment 1 reanalyzed EEG data from 23 participants who performed a visual search task (identifying a vertical or horizontal bar among distractors) in easy and hard conditions across 30 blocks of 64 trials. Behavioral data were analyzed using two-way repeated-measures ANOVAs and linear regression slopes examining intertrial target distance effects on response times and accuracy. Inverted Encoding Models (IEMs) were applied to EEG voltage data to reconstruct channel tuning functions (CTFs) tracking the previous trial's target location (n-1) across time, using a leave-one-set-out cross-validation procedure with 100 iterations. Trials where current and previous target locations matched were excluded. A derivative-based IEM analysis (sample-to-sample voltage changes) was conducted to rule out baseline correction artifacts. Searchlight analyses iteratively selected neighboring electrode groups to map scalp topography of spatial selectivity. Eye movement control analyses were also performed. Experiment 2 reanalyzed EEG data from 42 participants who performed a cued visual selection task with either a 100%-valid spatial cue (covert condition) or a neutral cue, across 32 blocks of 64 trials. Behavioral analyses using t-tests and repeated-measures ANOVAs examined intertrial priming on response times and accuracy separately for covert and neutral blocks. IEMs were applied to track previous target location reactivation in both cue conditions across time. Time-resolved Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA) was applied in both experiments to simultaneously and independently track neural representations of previous and current target locations. Theoretical representational dissimilarity matrices (RDMs) based on spatial distance between target locations were constructed, cross-validated Mahalanobis distances were computed from EEG voltage data binned in 20 ms windows, and semi-partial rank correlations isolated the unique variance explained by previous versus current target location. Statistical inference throughout used cluster-based permutation tests (one-tailed or two-tailed as appropriate, 10,000 iterations, α = .05).
